title: Latlas

seo.title: Latlas - daily geography game for iOS - Nattskift Games
seo.description: Latlas drops you on a real street somewhere on Earth. Look around, drop a pin, see how close you got. A new five-place daily, free, no ads, no account.
seo.supportDescription: Support for Latlas on iOS: the daily challenge, streaks, the Atlas globe, Game Center leaderboards, reminders, and how to reach the developer.
seo.privacyDescription: The Latlas privacy policy in plain language: the game collects nothing itself. No accounts, no analytics, no advertising. Street View imagery comes from Google.

hook: Dropped somewhere on Earth. Work out where.
pitch: Latlas puts you on a real street somewhere in the world. Look around, read the signs, notice which side the cars drive on, then drop your pin on the map. Every day brings the same five places for everyone, plus a neighborhood to guess in one of 11 cities. A globe fills in as you visit new countries. Free, no ads, no account.

keyArt.alt: A glowing glass globe showing the Americas with one orange map pin, ringed by six floating windows of roads around the world: a desert highway, a narrow European lane, a tropical coast road, a city boulevard, an alpine pass and a snowy mountain road.

appIcon.alt: Latlas app icon: a glowing glass globe with an orange map pin.

pillars.title: Real streets, official imagery
pillars.body: Thousands of places in more than a hundred countries, every one checked against Google's own Street View coverage. No blurry amateur photospheres: only official imagery, picked and verified before it ships.
pillars.alt: A straight outback road through red earth under a pale blue sky, as shown in a Latlas round.

pillars.title: Five places a day, the same for everyone
pillars.body: The daily is five rounds and one try, identical for every player. Keep your streak, compare notes with a friend, and share a score card that never gives the places away.
pillars.alt: The Latlas daily card: Challenge number 38, five places, same for everyone, one try, with a Play today button.

pillars.title: A world that fills in
pillars.body: The Atlas is a globe you can turn. Every country you have stood in lights up, grouped by continent, so you can see at a glance where you have never been.
pillars.alt: A turnable globe in the Atlas tab, with the Americas highlighted in bright cyan as visited countries.

screenshots.alt: A Street View round: a long straight road across red desert, with a Place your guess button below.
The guess map: a dark world map with a pin placed and a button to lock in the guess.
The result sheet: Australia, 3,079 points, 723 kilometres away, with a clue for the country.
The game summary: five rounds scored on a map with your guesses joined to the real places.
The Atlas tab: a globe of visited countries and a list grouped by continent.
The Stats tab: games played, best game and average score, then career figures such as rounds played, best single round, closest guess and countries seen.

deal.free: All of it: the daily challenge, free play with or without a clock, the theme of the week, Guess the neighborhood in 11 cities, the Atlas, your stats, Game Center leaderboards and a home screen widget.
deal.paid: Latlas Plus, a one-time unlock for people who play every day: the full archive of past dailies (the last week is free for everyone), trends in your stats, two more share-card styles, alternate icons and a supporter badge. There is also a tip jar; tips unlock nothing.
deal.costs: Nothing to play, and there are no ads to sit through. The imagery comes from Google over the internet, so it uses a little mobile data.
never: No account, no sign-up, and no email address needed to play.
No analytics or tracking of any kind from the studio.
No paywall on the daily or on free play, ever.

facts.languages: English, Spanish, German, French, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, Ukrainian

support.responseTime: Replies usually within a day or two. Include your iPhone model, iOS version and what the screen showed when it went wrong. The Contact us row in Settings fills in the details for you.

faq.a: Latlas needs an internet connection, because the imagery comes from Google rather than from inside the app. If a round sits on a dark screen, check your connection first. If it keeps happening on a good connection, tell us roughly when it happened.
No. The locations are built into the app, but the pictures are not - every panorama is fetched from Google when the round starts.

faq.q: How does the daily challenge work?
faq.a: Every day there is one numbered challenge, the same five places for everyone. Missed days can be caught up from the archive. Your streak counts days played in a row; giving up a daily part-way breaks it.

faq.q: The clock ran out before I guessed.
faq.a: Whatever pin is on the map when time runs out is submitted. With no pin, the round scores nothing. The clock does not start until the panorama has appeared, so a slow connection does not eat your thinking time, and it keeps running while the map is open.

faq.q: I lost my stats, or got a new iPhone.
faq.a: Game history is kept on your iPhone. Your daily-challenge progress and streak also sync through your own iCloud account if you are signed in, and Game Center keeps your leaderboard scores and achievements under your Game Center name. Without iCloud, history lost with a phone cannot be restored - there is no account and no server of ours holding a copy.

faq.q: Why is my best score split up?
faq.a: Bests are kept separately for each time limit. A score set with no clock is not the same achievement as one set under thirty seconds, so they are not compared.

faq.q: The place name showed for a moment.
faq.a: It should not. If you ever see the name of the place while a round is still being played, that is a bug worth reporting - tell us what you saw and roughly where the round turned out to be.

faq.q: Can I turn the sound off?
faq.a: Yes, in Settings. The game also respects the silent switch, and it never interrupts music or a podcast you already have playing.

faq.q: Why are some places so remote?
faq.a: Locations come from places with official Street View coverage, which means plenty of empty road. That is the game: a stretch of nothing still tells you which part of the world you are in, if you read it carefully.

Latlas is free, with no ads. Version 1.1 added optional extras: Latlas Plus, a one-time purchase that unlocks the full archive of past dailies, trends in your stats, two more share-card styles, alternate icons and a supporter badge, and a tip jar for anyone who just wants to say thanks. The daily challenge, free play, the theme of the week and the neighborhood game are free for everyone and will never be put behind a paywall.

faq.q: Can it remind me about the daily challenge?
faq.a: Yes: turn on New challenge alerts in Settings. The reminder is scheduled on your iPhone, not sent from a server, and can be turned off there or in the iPhone Settings app.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body: We collect nothing ourselves. There are no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking, and nothing about you is ever sent to us. Latlas does need the internet, because the imagery comes from Google, so Google sees those requests, and from version 1.1 GitHub sees a request for the theme file - explained below rather than buried.

sections.heading: What stays on your iPhone
sections.body: The game saves your finished games (score, date, time limit and each round's result), the stats worked out from them, and your settings. Two Apple services can carry a little of it: if you are signed in to iCloud, your daily-challenge progress and streak sync through your own iCloud account, and if you use Game Center, your scores go to Apple's Game Center under your Game Center name. Apple holds that data under Apple's own privacy policy; we never receive it.

sections.heading: Google Maps and Street View
sections.body: The panoramas and the world map come from Google. When a round loads, your iPhone asks Google for the imagery directly, and Google receives what it needs to answer, including your IP address. We send Google nothing about you, and nothing in that exchange passes through us. That use is governed by the Google Maps/Google Earth Additional Terms of Service and the Google Privacy Policy.

sections.heading: What Google's software collects
sections.body: Latlas includes Google's Maps software, which collects some data for Google, not for us. Google's disclosure for it lists a device identifier and other technical data, linked to the device and used for analytics and to make the maps work, and crash, performance and basic interaction data, not linked to you. Google states none of it is used for tracking. We do not receive it.

sections.heading: Theme updates
sections.body: From version 1.1, Latlas occasionally downloads a small public text file from this game's page on GitHub Pages (pacificfrontdesk.github.io/latlas). It lists extra weekly themes: a title, an icon name and a list of countries. Your iPhone asks for the file directly, so GitHub receives the request, including your IP address, under GitHub's own privacy statement. The request carries nothing about you or your games, and the file is only read, never run. The app keeps the last copy on your iPhone so it keeps working offline.

sections.heading: Notifications
sections.body: If you turn on New challenge alerts, the reminder is scheduled on your iPhone itself; nothing is sent from a server. Turn it off in the game's Settings or the iPhone Settings app.

sections.heading: Where you are
sections.body: Latlas never asks for your location and does not use it. The game is about guessing where the picture is, not where you are.

sections.heading: Children
sections.body: Latlas is suitable for children. It collects nothing, so there is nothing to collect from a child. Street View imagery is real photography of public places, shown as Google provides it.

sections.heading: Changes
sections.body: Version 1.1 added optional purchases (Latlas Plus and tips). Apple processes them; we never see your payment details, and the app keeps only whether Plus is unlocked, on your device. If a future version collects anything else or adds advertising, this page and the App Store privacy label will be updated before that version ships. Latlas is published by Pacific Front Desk LLC, doing business as Nattskift Games.

sections.body: Latlas is licensed to you, not sold, under Apple's standard Licensed Application End User License Agreement together with these terms. You may use it on devices linked to your Apple Account, for personal, non-commercial purposes. You may not copy, resell, reverse-engineer or redistribute it.

sections.heading: Imagery from Google
sections.body: The panoramas and maps are Google Maps content, shown through Google's own services, and your use of them is also subject to the Google Maps/Google Earth Additional Terms of Service and the Google Privacy Policy. The app does not store or copy the imagery; you may not extract, save or redistribute it from Latlas, and Google's attribution must not be obscured.

sections.heading: Scores, stats and Game Center
sections.body: Game history is kept on your iPhone, daily progress may sync through your iCloud account, and leaderboard scores go to Apple Game Center. None of it is guaranteed against data loss, device changes or reinstalling the app, and we hold no copy to restore.

sections.heading: Purchases
sections.body: Latlas is free to download and play. Since version 1.1 it offers optional in-app purchases: Latlas Plus, a one-time unlock, and tips. They are processed by Apple under the Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions, shown with their price before you buy, and refunded by Apple at reportaproblem.apple.com. A tip unlocks nothing; Plus adds extras and never gates the daily challenge or free play.

sections.heading: Availability
sections.body: The game is provided as it is. We do not promise it will be free of faults, available without interruption, or supported forever. Latlas needs an internet connection and depends on Google's services, so rounds may fail to load for reasons outside our hands.

sections.heading: Liability
sections.body: To the fullest extent permitted by law, Pacific Front Desk LLC is not liable for any indirect or consequential loss arising from use of the app. Nothing here limits rights you have under consumer law in your own country.
